steps.prompt: Their C has the puck in our corner and looks up. What does their team want?

options.text: A shot with nobody in its way
options.fb: Right. From the corner there is no angle, so the puck has to move first: up the wall to the point, or D-to-D to the other point.

options.text: A goal straight from the corner
options.fb: From the corner there is almost no net to shoot at. Their C moves the puck to a player with a clear shot, most often at the point.

options.text: Time with the puck in the corner
options.fb: They take time there only until a pass opens up. Time in the corner scores nothing; the pass to a player with a clear shot is what they want.

steps.prompt: Their C passes up the wall to their LD at the point. Whose job is their LD?

options.text: Our RW, the winger on that side
options.fb: Right. Our RW is already between the puck and their LD. They arrive as the pass does, and the shot has to go through them.

options.text: Our RD, from the fight in the corner
options.fb: Our RD's job is the puck in the corner. From there they are ten meters below the point, and their LD shoots while they skate.

options.text: Our C, out of the slot
options.fb: Our C could get there, but late, and the slot is empty behind them. Their LW waits there for a pass and a shot from close.

options.text: Nobody, everyone helps at the puck
options.fb: Watch what happens. With our RW down at the puck, nobody is in the lane to the point. Their LD gets the pass alone and shoots.

steps.prompt: The pass is leaving for the point. Tap where our RW should be.

fb.right: Right. Above the puck, between it and their LD, in the lane up the wall. The pass has to go through our RW.
fb.close: Near the lane, but a stride off it. That stride gives their LD time to look up and pick a shot.
fb.wrong: Too far from the lane. Our RW stands between the puck and their LD, a few strides from the point.
